html:
SMTO-EML-0012 — Your mail server can't handle an address with special letters

GUID: 09f7e223-e322-5a58-8cfd-555dec7d49c1
Slug: email-smtputf8-unsupported
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • An email address in this message uses accented or non-English letters before the @ sign, and your mail server doesn't support those. SMTO stopped before sending, so nothing went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the recipient addresses for letters such as é, ü or non-Latin characters before the @ sign, and ask those recipients for a plain-letter address if they have one. Only the part before the @ causes this; special letters after the @ are converted automatically.
  2. If the sender or reply-to address in your sender profile has such letters, ask the person who manages SMTO to change it to a plain-letter address in Parameter Store. The sender's own address must also be one your mail server can handle.
  3. Otherwise, ask your email administrator for a mail server that supports international addresses (called SMTPUTF8) and have the sender profile use it. A server with that support can deliver addresses with special letters.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your email administrator or the person who manages SMTO, noting which address uses special letters.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The message requires SMTPUTF8 (a non-ASCII local part in a sender, reply-to or recipient address), but the SMTP server does not advertise both SMTPUTF8 and 8BITMIME.

What this means

  • A message requiring SMTPUTF8 reaches a server that lacks SMTPUTF8 or 8BITMIME advertisement. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • A message requiring SMTPUTF8 reaches a server that lacks SMTPUTF8 or 8BITMIME advertisement.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the envelope's Unicode local parts and both advertised SMTP extensions; Unicode domains have a separate IDNA conversion.

How to fix it

  • Use ASCII local parts in the from_email, envelope_from, reply_to and recipient addresses, or point the email_smtp profile at an SMTP server that advertises SMTPUTF8 and 8BITMIME. Unicode domains are already converted with IDNA and are not the cause.
  • Use ASCII local parts in addresses or select a server supporting SMTPUTF8. Unicode domains are converted with IDNA.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended addresses use a supported server or deliberate ASCII local-part alternatives.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
